record.paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
record.original_question: How can future detections of EeV-energy cosmogenic or point-source neutrinos be used to test neutrino-nucleon cross sections, neutrino flavor composition, Lorentz-violation-like effects, neutrino decay, equivalence-principle violation, or other new physics over gigaparsec baselines, while separating fundamental effects from astrophysical uncertainties in spectra, source evolution, arrival directions, and flavor identification?

evidence.quote: Cosmogenic neutrinos, with EeV energies, when discovered, could extend the reach of these tests.

Cosmogenic neutrinos could be used to measure the cross section at the EeV scale for the ﬁrst time, test strong dynamics more deeply than colliders [351, 352], and search for new physics at an even higher energy scale.

New physics of different types can affect all neutrino observables: the energy spectrum (see, e.g., [368–374]), distribution of arrival directions (see,e.g., [375, 376]), and the ﬂavor composition, i.e., the proportion of each neutrino ﬂavor to the total in the incoming ﬂux (see, e.g., [377–380]).

Numerous new-physics models have effects that are proportional to some power of the neutrino energyE and to the propagated distance L, i.e., they grow as∼ κnEnL, where the energy dependence n and the proportionality constant κn are model-dependent.

For instance, for neutrino decay [353–355], n =−1; for CPT-odd Lorentz violation [356–358] or coupling to a torsion ﬁeld [359], n = 0; and for CPT-even Lorentz violation [360, 361] or violation of the equivalence principle [362–365], n = 1.

When extracting fundamental neutrino properties from the data, one must factor in astrophysical uncertainties (e.g., shape of the energy spectrum, redshift evolution of the number density of sources, etc.), which can be signiﬁcant;
Action item 8: Generate updated predictions of the emission of UHE neutrinos from point sources, steady-state and transient.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an isotropic diffuse flux of ultra-high-energy (EeV-scale) neutrinos consisting of (i) a cosmogenic component produced by interactions of ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray protons and nuclei with the cosmic microwave and infrared backgrounds during propagation over cosmological (gigaparsec) baselines, and (ii) a possible point-source component from identified astrophysical accelerators. For such neutrinos, the observable quantities at Earth are: the energy spectrum dN/dE, the distribution of arrival directions on the sky, and the flavor composition (f_e : f_μ : f_τ) of the incoming flux after oscillations.

Assume that beyond-Standard-Model effects modify neutrino propagation and/or interactions in such a way that the deviation of an observable from its Standard-Model expectation can be parametrized in the schematic form
   Δ𝒪(E, L) ≃ κ_n · E^n · L,
where E is the neutrino energy, L the propagation baseline, n ∈ ℤ a model-dependent integer (e.g. n = −1 for neutrino decay, n = 0 for equivalence-principle violation, n ≥ 1 for Lorentz-invariance-violating dispersion relations), and κ_n a model-dependent coupling. Likewise, the neutrino–nucleon cross section σ_{νN}(E) at center-of-mass energies above those reached at terrestrial colliders may deviate from QCD extrapolations.

Develop a quantitative statistical framework that, given an assumed exposure of a future EeV neutrino observatory and assumed astrophysical priors on (a) the source spectral index and maximum energy, (b) the redshift evolution of source density, (c) the cosmic-ray mass composition feeding cosmogenic production, and (d) the flavor composition at the source, determines:

1. The minimum number of detected EeV cosmogenic and/or point-source neutrino events required to measure σ_{νN}(E) at E ∼ 10^{18} eV with a prescribed relative precision, and to distinguish Standard-Model QCD predictions from new high-energy strong-dynamics scenarios.

2. The sensitivity reach (i.e. smallest |κ_n| that can be excluded at a given confidence level) for each integer n ∈ {−1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4} from the joint analysis of spectrum, arrival-direction distribution, and flavor ratios.

3. A procedure to disentangle a putative new-physics signal in any of these observables from astrophysical degeneracies in spectral shape, source evolution, sky distribution, and flavor identification, including a quantitative criterion (e.g. an information-theoretic or likelihood-ratio criterion) under which fundamental and astrophysical effects become separable.

Provide explicit predicted bounds, identify the observable channel (spectrum, arrival directions, or flavor composition) that yields the strongest constraint for each n, and characterize the irreducible astrophysical uncertainty floor below which no improvement in detector exposure can refine the test.
artifact.status_search_result: EeV-energy cosmogenic neutrinos have not yet been detected; experiments such as IceCube-Gen2, GRAND, POEMMA, RNO-G, and the Pierre Auger Observatory continue to push upper limits but no confirmed cosmogenic neutrino flux exists as of 2026. Consequently the proposed program of using EeV neutrinos to test cross sections, flavor composition, Lorentz violation, neutrino decay, and equivalence-principle violation over gigaparsec baselines remains an open research direction, with only forecast/sensitivity studies available rather than measurements.

status_evidence.title: IceCube-Gen2 Technical Design Report
status_evidence.snippet: IceCube-Gen2 aims to detect the cosmogenic neutrino flux at EeV energies; no detection has yet been made.
status_evidence.claim: Cosmogenic EeV neutrinos remain undetected; their detection is a future goal.

status_evidence.title: Pierre Auger Collaboration, limits on UHE neutrinos
status_evidence.snippet: We present updated upper limits on the diffuse flux of ultra-high-energy neutrinos; no candidate events observed.
status_evidence.claim: Current experimental status is upper limits, not detection, supporting the open status of EeV neutrino new-physics tests.

status_evidence.title: GRAND Collaboration science case
status_evidence.snippet: GRAND will probe new physics with EeV neutrinos including Lorentz violation, neutrino decay, and cross-section measurements.
status_evidence.claim: Tests of new physics with EeV neutrinos are forecast goals, not completed measurements.
